rebaseline_note:
ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.10 (2026-08-11, ENGINE-tier, ZERO grammar bytes, generated parsers BYTE-IDENTICAL): expected_union_unknown 2 -> 1 and expected_canonical_unknown 13 -> 12 — the A2.5 debt PARTIALLY repaid. `block_event_expression_lr_suffix` now WITNESSES; `select_expression_lr_suffix` remains, for a DIFFERENT and separately-diagnosed reason (below). expected_canonical_witness 1343 -> 1344, expected_union_witness 1354 -> 1355; expected_total 1362, expected_proof 6 and sample_parse_failures=0 all UNCHANGED.

⛔ THIS NOTE CORRECTS THE ROOT CAUSE THE A2.5 NOTE RECORDED, which was wrong and would have sent the next session to the wrong file. A2.5 wrote: 'the rule-target reach planner cannot route to a rule that did not exist when the reach graph was built'. MEASURED FALSE. `reach_hops_pass` BFSes `self.grammar_tree` AFTER elimination, so the synthetic rules are in its graph, and `PGEN_REACH_PATH_DUMP=1` prints a COMPLETE and CORRECT 21-hop chain ending `("bins_selection_or_option","root/o1/s1"), ("bins_selection","root/s3"), ("select_expression","root/s1/q")` — the plan already steered every OR and already forced the LR quantifier. The plan was never the defect; RENDERING it was.

REAL ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE, tools-first, reproduced on an 11-rule synthetic before SV was touched). `generate_quantified` (rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs) looked up `forced_quantifier_min` by `(current_rule, node_path)` with NO call-stack re-entry guard — unlike `generate_or`, which has carried exactly that guard since RTL-FE-CLOSURE.5.6 (`suppress_recursive_forced_branch`). LR elimination emits `X := X_lr_base ( X_lr_suffix )*` with `X_lr_suffix := op X`, so the forced site's own body RE-ENTERS the rule that owns the site: every re-entry re-forced the `*`. `PGEN_TRACE_VERBOSITY=high` counted 119 forced decisions at site `expr::root/s1` in a SINGLE probe. The derivation never terminates, the forced branch dies on depth, and `generate_or`'s forced-first-WITH-fallback then silently renders a sibling — which is why the probe sample showed `option.f = 3.5` (the sibling) rather than anything near the target. ⇒ left recursion was UNWITNESSABLE BY CONSTRUCTION for every grammar, not just SystemVerilog.

THE FIX. `generate_quantified` now stands the forced minimum down on a genuine re-entry (>=2 live occurrences of `current_rule` on the call stack) when the quantified element can reach back into `current_rule` — scoped exactly like the OR guard, so every non-recursive forced quantifier is byte-identical. Pinned by two lib tests: `forced_quantifier_stands_down_on_re_entry_so_an_lr_suffix_can_witness` (proven DISCRIMINATING — RED with the guard disabled, reproducing the exact production symptom) and `re_entry_guard_leaves_a_non_recursive_forced_quantifier_alone` (the monotonicity control).

⭐ THE RESIDUAL `select_expression_lr_suffix` IS NOW A SECOND, DISTINCT MECHANISM — recorded here so it is not mistaken for the same defect. Post-fix the generator emits the STRUCTURALLY CORRECT probe `cross f, f { bins f = f && f; }`, i.e. it does reach and render the `&&` continuation. It still reports `witnessed_target=false` because the PARSER does not commit to it: `select_expression`'s catch-all arm `cross_set_expression -> covergroup_expression -> expression` is the full SV expression hierarchy, which parses `&&`/`||` ITSELF, so under longest-match the seed swallows the whole operand and the `( _lr_suffix )*` never commits. Measured: `--parse-dump-ast-pretty` on that exact shape yields kind `cross_set`, never `and`. This is the same fact `stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/fixed_select_expression_paren.sv` already documents in prose ('parentheses around an operand carrying no `intersect` prove nothing'), which is why every pinned reproducer uses a `binsof(...) intersect {...}` operand. ⇒ what is owed is SEED diversification: when the target is `X_lr_suffix`, the witness planner must also steer `X_lr_base`'s own alternatives, because a seed that the longest-match catch-all can absorb makes the suffix unwitnessable regardless of how well the path is forced. Owned by ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.10, which stays OPEN and remains the named blocker for returning this basis to 0.

GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.A2.5 (2026-08-11, ENGINE-tier, ZERO grammar bytes): ⛔⛔ THIS RE-BASELINE MOVES expected_union_unknown 0 -> 2, AND THAT IS A REGRESSION IN THIS BASIS, RECORDED AS ONE RATHER THAN ABSORBED. It is NOT a cap raised to admit content: the two rules are named, their cause is root-caused tools-first, and the defect that produces them is OWNED by ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.10, which is the named blocker for returning this basis to 0.

WHAT CHANGED. A2.5 taught LR elimination the DIRECT shape (`A := A op B | ...`), so `select_expression` and `block_event_expression` now carry LR plans where they carried none. Every LR plan synthesizes a `<rule>_lr_base` / `<rule>_lr_suffix` pair, so the census gains 4 rules: expected_total 1358 -> 1362, expected_canonical_witness 1341 -> 1343, expected_union_witness 1352 -> 1354. The two `_lr_base` rules witness normally. The two `_lr_suffix` rules do NOT: expected_canonical_unknown 11 -> 13 and expected_union_unknown 0 -> 2, residual ["block_event_expression_lr_suffix","select_expression_lr_suffix"]. Deterministic (byte-identical) across seeds 0/7/42; expected_proof stays 6; sample_parse_failures stay 0.

ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE, tools-first, NOT a guess). `PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES=1` reports both rules `parsed=true witnessed_target=false` — the probe's sample PARSES but does not reach the target. Reading the samples names the miss exactly: for `select_expression_lr_suffix` the generator emits `cross f, f { option.f = 3.5; }` — the `option` arm of `cross_body_item`, which never enters `bins_selection` and so never reaches `select_expression` at all; for `block_event_expression_lr_suffix` it emits `covergroup f @f_0 ;` — `coverage_event`'s simple `@` form, not the `@@( ... )` block-event form. The rule-target reach planner cannot route to a rule that did not exist when the reach graph was built, and `_lr_suffix` is synthesized by elimination.

⭐ GROUND TRUTH SAYS THE RULES ARE LIVE, so this is an INSTRUMENT gap, not a dead-rule finding — the distinction that decides whether a `parsed=true witnessed_target=false` verdict means 'delete the rule' (the v5 engine-shadowed-dead precedent) or 'fix the generator'. Four adjudication reproducers exercise these exact continuations through the REAL generated parser and pass with their arms pinned: fixed_select_expression_{with,paren,or}.sv (arms `with_matches`, `and>paren`, `or>paren`) and fixed_block_event_or.sv (arm `or`). A rule that four pinned reproducers demonstrably reach is not uncovered; it is unwitnessed BY THIS GENERATOR.

⚠️ PRECEDENT, and why it does not apply. Contract v6 (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.6.1) removed a `module_path_expression_lr_suffix` UNKNOWN by making its producer natively non-left-recursive, i.e. by DELETING the LR plan. That option is closed here by the director's 2026-08-11 ruling: the engine handles what is common to all EBNFs, so avoiding LR plans to keep a census clean would re-introduce exactly the hand-compilation A2.5 exists to remove. The census must learn to witness engine-synthesized rules.

done_rule: SV is recognized fully_certified when the multi-config certificate-coverage union UNKNOWN reaches 0. Until then the recognized fully_certified-accounting basis is the sound multi-config union (expected_union_unknown), whose residual rule set must equal expected_union_residual_rules exactly (order-insensitive) and be deterministic (byte-identical) across all declared seeds, with sample_parse_failures=0; the canonical single-config accounting (expected_canonical_unknown) is recorded alongside. The union is sound by construction: a rule is credited only when some config POSITIVELY covers it (a proof or a witness — including the VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.7 per-profile ProfileEntryUnreachable/ProfileUnproducibleGate proofs, each independently re-derived), never merely because a profile leaves the rule out of its universe.
